title: A SILVER-MOUNTED IVORY FLUTE by WHITAKER & Co., London, stamped on the joints with the date 1819. With tuning head, six hexagonal silver keys. Length from centre of embouchure to foot base 23 1/4" (590 mm). Expansion crack in he head joint crossing the embouchure. With contemporary mahogany case.

A FLUTE by MONZANI & Co., stamped on the joints HILL late MONZANI & Co., 28 Regent Street, Piccadilly, London, 3164. With tuning head, the silver mounts and keys stamped with the crown hallmark date 1835. Eight keys with circular flaps (minus holding screw for foot key flap). Overall length 23" (585 mm). Expansion crack in the small barrel. With original fitted case.

A FLUTE by MONZANI & Co., stamped HILL late MONZANI & Co., 28 Regent Street, Piccadilly, London, 3232. With tuning head, the silver mounts plain, silver lip-plate. Eight keys, one with double touch stamped with the hallmark date 1836. Length from centre of embouchure to foot base 23 1/8" (587 mm). Expansion crack in the head joint. With mahogany case.

AN IVORY-MOUNTED BOXWOOD FLUTE by FIRTH, HALL & POND, New York, circa 1840. With four brass spoon keys (one minus touch). Length from centre of embouchure to foot joint 20 13/16" (530 mm), in case. Minus ivory foot-collar.
AN EBONY TREBLE RECORDER bearing an indecipherable stamp. Overall length 19 3/4" (502 mm).

A NICKEL-MOUNTED EBONITE FLUTE by BOOSEY & Co., London, No. 14982. THE R. S. PRATTENS PERFECTED. Last quarter 19th century. Length from centre of embouchure to foot joint 22 5/8" (575 mm), with cleaning rod, in wood case.
A NICKEL-MOUNTED EBONY OBOE by CABART, Paris. Overall length 23 7/8" (605 mm). Excellent condition. With a fitted carry-case.
A NICKEL-MOUNTED EBONITE CLARINET, Boehm system. Engraved COUTURE, Paris, on the bell. Overall length, including mouthpiece, 26 1/8" (604 mm). With case.

A NICKEL-MOUNTED Concert Flute by RUDALL CARTE & Co., 23 Berners Street, London; Boehm system, covered holes, closed G sharp, with case. AN EBONITE CONCERT FLUTE, Boehm system, open G sharp, in case. And A CONCERT FLUTE by HAWKES & SON, Denman Street, London; nickel mounts on rosewood, with a case by HAWKES & SON. (3)

A CONCERT FLUTE by RUDALL CARTE & Co., 23 Berners Street, Oxford Street, London, No. 6152, the 1867 patent. Open G sharp, Boehm system, thinned, head, ebony lip-plate. Length from centre of embouchure to foot base 23 5/8" (600 mm). An expansion crack in lower part of the head. With case and cleaning rod.
A NICKEL-MOUNTED ROSEWOOD COR ANGLAIS by JACQUES ALBERT of Brussels, with two crooks. Overall length without crook 30" (762 mm). With fitted carry-case.
A NICKEL-MOUNTED EBONY OBOE by JULIUS HEINRICH ZIMMERMANN in Leipzig. Continental system. Overall length minus reed 22 7/8" (582 mm). With fitted case.
A NICKEL-MOUNTED ROSEWOOD OBOE by HAWKES & SON, London, EXCELSIOR SONORUS CLASS, 6881. Simple system. Overall length minus reed 21 1/4" (540 mm).
A STAINED BOXWOOD FLUTE, circa 1800, stamped MILLIGAN, London. Of four joints with ivory mounts, one square brass key. Length from centre of embouchure to foot base 17 3/16" (437 mm).
A NICKEL-MOUNTED EBONY WITH ROSEWOOD BELL CLARINET, bearing the brand KARL MEYER. Boehm system. Overall length 26" (660 mm), with mouthpiece protector and box.

A VIOLIN by H. EMILE BLONDELET, bearing the maker's label LUTHIER A PARIS, dated Année 1924. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), with a bow, in a shaped leather grained case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a transparent orange colour.

A VIOLIN by ARISTIDE CAVALLI, bearing the maker's label OFFICINA CLAUDIO MONTEVERDE, CREMONA, dated 1923 with the signature GIO. MARIA CERUTI. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), in a modern oblong black cloth-covered violin case lined green velvet. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to medium on the flanks, the varnish of a red-amber colour (two repairs on left flanks of the table).

A CARLO STORIONI VIOLIN, bearing the maker's label CREMONENSIS, FACIEBAT 1897. L.O.B. 14 1/16" (357 mm). The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong broad grain, the varnish of a clear brown shade.

A SAXON VIOLIN, circa 1780, of the MEINAL SCHOOL. L.O.B. 14" (356 mm), with a silver-mounted bow, in a shaped oak case lined blue velvet. The one-piece back of faint broad curl, the ribs similar, the scroll plain, the table showing broad grain on the left flank, narrowing to the right flank, the varnish of a golden-brown colour.

AN INTERESTING GERMAN VIOLIN, circa 1840. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), with a silver-mounted bow, the adjuster of nickel, in shaped case. The two-piece back cut on the slab showing narrow mottled figure, the ribs of similar wood, the scroll of narrow curl, the table of medium grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of an opaque brown colour on a light brown ground. A small repair in the upper left rib.

A GOOD VIOLIN by FRANCOIS SALZARD, circa 1850, bearing the maker's label with decorative border in Paris. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm). The one-piece back of medium curl, the ribs similar, the scroll plain, the table of broad grain, the varnish of a transparent golden-yellow colour.

A VIOLIN of the NEUNER SCHOOL, circa 1870. L.O.B. 14" (356 mm). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of narrow curl, the table of narrow grain widening to medium on the flanks, the varnish of a light red-brown colour on a yellow ground.

A GERMAN VIOLIN, circa 1790. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), in case. The one-piece back, of medium curl, the ribs of narrow medium curl, the scroll of medium curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a light red-brown colour.

A VIOLIN by FRANCOIS BARZONI, bearing the maker's label dated 1897 and branded F.B. on the button. L.O.B. 14 1/16" (357 mm), with a bow, in case. The two-piece back, ribs and scroll of medium figure, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a transparent red-brown colour. A repair on table left lower flank.

A FRENCH VIOLIN of the COLIN SCHOOL, circa 1900, bearing the label of WOLFF BROS., dated 1897. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), with a bow, in case. The attractive two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain widening to the flanks, the transparent varnish of a red colour on a yellow ground.
A MUTE VIOLIN by F. W. PRIESTLY, circa 1978, in case. The body of mahogany of skeleton outline, the maker's initials inset a metal disk on the button.

A VIOLIN by GULIELMUS PIKE, bearing the maker's label DE EXON, dated anno 1944 and in script 2nd Front, June 6th, Normandy. L.O.B. 13 7/8" (353 mm), in a rosewood-veneer case by W. E. Hill & Sons. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the transparent varnish of a golden-amber colour.

A VIOLIN by GULIELMUS PIKE, bearing the maker's label DE OXON, dated anno 1929. L.O.B. 14" (356 mm), in case. The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of an orange-red colour on a yellow ground. Worm marks in the bottom rib and the scroll.

A GERMAN VIOLIN of the HOYER SCHOOL, circa 1800. L.O.B. 14 1/4" (362 mm). The two-piece back cut on the slab showing faint curl, the ribs and scroll plain, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of a golden-brown colour.

A VIOLIN by SILVIO SPARGNAFANI, bearing the maker's label in Basel, anno 1973, Opus 2 unter Anleitung von T. NEMETH, Geigenbaur gefertigt. L.O.B. 14 3/16" (360 mm). The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll similar figure, the table of medium grain narrowing to the flanks, the varnish of a light red-brown colour on a yellow ground.

A COMPOSITE VIOLIN, the back and ribs circa 1780 in the manner of Charles Harris, the table circa 1800 (English), the scroll (English) circa 1900. L.O.B. 13 7/8" (353 mm), in wood case. The one-piece back and ribs of attractive narrow curl, the table of narrow grain, the scroll of narrow curl, the varnish of a golden red-brown colour on a light brown ground.

A GOOD ENGLISH VIOLIN, circa 1780, of the BERNHARD FENDT SCHOOL. L.O.B. 13 13/16" (352 mm). The one-piece back cut on the slab showing narrow curl ascending to the right, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of broad grain, the varnish of a deep red-brown colour on a light brown ground.
A VIOLIN BOW by JOHN DODD, stamped on the shaft and frog. The ebony frog with pearl eye, unlined, the round stick with ebony face of a red-brown colour. The nickel adjuster modern.

A KLINGENTHAL VIOLA, circa 1910. L.O.B. 15 3/8" (392 mm), with a bow, in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of broad curl, the table of strong broad grain, the varnish of a golden-brown colour.

A MIRECOURT VIOLIN, circa 1890, labelled MAGGINI. L.O.B. 14 1/2" (369 mm), in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of an orange-brown colour. Double purfled.

A BAVARIAN VIOLIN, circa 1860. L.O.B. 14 3/16" (360 mm), with a silver-mounted bow, in case and cover. The two-piece back and ribs of narrow figure, the scroll plain, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a red-brown colour.

A FRENCH VIOLIN of the COLIN SCHOOL, circa 1900. L.O.B. 14 1/4" (362 mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour.

A FRENCH VIOLIN by HAWKES & SON, London, bearing the maker's label "THE CONCERT VIOLIN", dated 1901. L.O.B. 14 3/16" (360 mm). The two-piece back and ribs of broad figure, the scroll of narrow curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a transparent orange colour.

A GERMAN VIOLIN, circa 1880. L.O.B. 14 1/16" (357 mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a transparent deep red-brown colour.

A GOOD MARKNEUKIRCHEN VIOLIN, circa 1880. L.O.B. 14" (356 mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong medium grain widening slightly to the flanks, the transparent varnish of a red colour on a brown ground.

A FRENCH VIOLIN, circa 1870, branded H. DERAZEY on the inner back. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), with a violin bow, stick faintly stamped LUPOT, in shaped wood case. The two-piece back of narrow flame ascending from the joint, the ribs of viola depth of similar figure, the scroll of faint figure, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a golden-orange colour. Minus tailpiece.

A VIOLIN of the CAUSSIN, VOSGES, SCHOOL, circa 1870. L.O.B. 13 7/8" (353 mm). The one-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll plain, the table of broad grain, the varnish of an orange colour.

A MARKNEUKIRCHEN VIOLIN, circa 1900, bearing label. L.O.B. 13 15/16" (354 mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong narrow grain, the clear varnish of a light brown colour.

A MIRECOURT VIOLIN, circa 1910. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of narrow curl, the table of narrow grain widening on the flanks, the varnish of a clear light orange colour. Minus tailpiece and top fingerboard nut. Model after GUARNERI.

A FLEMISH VIOLIN, the back, ribs and scroll circa 1780. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm). The two-piece back and ribs of narrow curl, the scroll plain, the table (circa 1800 of the HOYER SCHOOL, Mittenwald) of narrow grain, the varnish of a golden-brown colour, the table darker.

AN INTERESTING FRENCH VIOLIN, circa 1760, the model after GRAGNANI and bearing a manuscript label. L.O.B. 14 1/16" (357 mm), with a bow with mother-of-pearl frog, in case. The two-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a golden-amber colour. (Some old worm marks in the back and ribs.)

A VIOLIN of the MATHIAS NEUNER SCHOOL, Mittenwald, circa 1830. L.O.B. 14 1/16" (357 mm), in case. The one-piece back of medium curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table showing medium grain on the left flank narrowing to the right flank, the oil varnish craquelled of a red-brown colour. (Table fair condition.)

A VIOLIN by FRANK DEVONEY, bearing the maker's label dated 1897. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), in case. The two-piece back of medium flame ascending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of medium grain, the oil varnish of an orange-brown colour on a yellow ground. (Neck loose from the block.)

A QUARTER-SIZE FRENCH VIOLIN, circa 1910. L.O.B. 10 1/2" (267 mm), with a bow, in case. The one-piece back, ribs and scroll of plain wood, the table of broad grain, the varnish of an orange colour. Minus two pegs.

A GOOD MIRECOURT VIOLIN, circa 1910, labelled CRAIGS CELEBRATED VIOLINS, dated Aberdeen 1912. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), with a nickel-mounted bow stamped J. KNOPF on the shaft, in case. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of broad grain, the varnish of a transparent orange colour.

A TYROLESE VIOLIN of the WIDHOLM SCHOOL, circa 1760, labelled MATTIO ALBAN, fecit Bolzan 1700. L.O.B. 13 3/4" (350 mm), with two bows (one stamped DODD), in a wood case, circa 1830, labelled EDWARD WITHERS. The one-piece back cut on the slab showing convoluted grain, the ribs and scroll plain, the table of narrow grain, the varnish of an opaque deep red colour on a brown ground.

A PARIS SCHOOL VIOLIN, circa 1850. L.O.B. 13 7/8" (352 mm), with two bows, in case. The one-piece back of broad curl, the ribs and scroll of similar wood, the table of medium grain, narrowing on the flanks, the varnish of a red-brown colour on an amber ground.

A VIOLIN of the SCHONBACH SCHOOL, circa 1910. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain narrowing to the flanks, the transparent varnish of an orange colour.

A KLINGENTHAL VIOLIN, circa 1770. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), in an oblong leather case. The two-piece back of unfigured wood, the ribs cut on the slab of faint figure, the scroll plain the table of medium and narrow grain, the varnish of a golden-brown colour.

AN ENGLISH VIOLIN, circa 1830, branded FORSTER, London, below the button. L.O.B. 14" (356 mm), with two bows, in shaped leather case. The one-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll plain, the table of medium grain narrowing on the flanks, the varnish of a clear golden-orange colour.

A VIOLIN by FRANCOIS BARZONI, bearing the maker's label at CHATEAU THIERY, dated 1886. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (360 mm), with a bow and case. The two-piece back, ribs and scroll of medium figure, the table of narrow grain, the clear varnish of a brown colour.

A MITTENWALD VIOLIN of the NEUNER MITTENWALD SCHOOL, circa 1860. L.O.B. 14 1/16" (357 mm). The one-piece back and scroll of unfigured wood, the ribs of faint narrow curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a light red-brown colour.

A THREEQUARTER-SIZE MITTENWALD VIOLIN, circa 1880. The one-piece back of faint narrow figure, the ribs and scroll plain, the table of open broad grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour. (Minus two pegs, an open table crack beneath the chin-rest.)

A FRENCH VIOLIN by JEAN BAPTISTE COLIN, bearing the label LUTHERIE ARTISTIQUE, année 1893, with a French bow (damaged) stamped PAJEOT, in a shaped velvet-lined wood case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar faint figure, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the clear varnish of an orange-red colour.

A FRENCH VIOLIN, circa 1880, labelled JOANNES FRANCISCUS PRESSENDA, Turin 1834. L.O.B. 14 5/16" (364 mm), with a bow by CHARLES HUSSON A PARIS stamped on the shaft, and another bow stamped LEON BERNARDEL, in a shaped black wood case. The one-piece back of medium to broad curl, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of broad grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground. (Some worm marks in neck and scroll.)

A VIOLIN by REGINALD G. PRICE, bearing the maker's manuscript label in Kingston, dated 1927. L.O.B. 14 1/16" (357 mm), with case. The one-piece back of medium curl ascending to the right, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table showing broad grain on the left flank narrowing to the right flank, the varnish of a golden-brown colour. Mint condition.

A GOOD PARIS SCHOOL VIOLIN, circa 1910. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), with a bow, in a shaped wood case by W. E. HILL & SONS, with cover. The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of an orange colour on a yellow ground.

A FRENCH VIOLIN, circa 1880, labelled COLLIN-MEZIN A PARIS 1884, with the receipt of MESSRS. J. P. GUIVER & Co. LTD., London, for a violin by J. B. COLLIN-MEZIN. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of medium grain widening to the flanks, the transparent varnish of brown-red colour.

A VIOLIN by THOMAS PERRY & WILLIAM WILKINSON, bearing the makers' label at No. 4, Anglesea Street, Dublin, dated 1817, with the brand PERRY, Dublin, below the button. L.O.B. 14" (355 mm), in a shaped wood case. The two-piece back of medium flame showing a faint water mark on the left flank, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll plain, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a clear red-brown colour on a light brown ground.

A GOOD CARLO STORIONI VIOLIN, bearing the maker's label CREMONENSIS FACIEBAT 1890. L.O.B. 14 3/16" (360 mm). The two-piece back of medium flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong broad grain, the varnish of an orange-brown colour on a yellow ground. Mint condition.

A VIOLIN bearing the label BENNETTINI, VIA S. GIOVANNI ALLA GONCA 49, MILANO, circa 1890. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), in case. The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong narrow grain, the varnish of a brown-amber colour.

A GOOD THREEQUARTER-SIZE MITTENWALD VIOLIN, circa 1860, labelled SIMPERTUS NIGGELL, Lauton und Geigenmacher in Füssen 1672. L.O.B. 13 1/8" (334 mm). with a silver-mounted bow, in case. The two-piece back of narrow curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong medium grain, the varnish of a red-brown colour.
A VIOLIN, circa 1780. L.O.B. 14 1/4" (362 mm), in case. The two-piece back of faint small figure, the ribs similar, the scroll plain, the table of broad grain, the varnish of a golden-brown colour.

A VIOLIN by GEORGE CRASKE, bearing the label MADE BY GEORGE CRASKE (born 1797, died 1888) and sold by WILLIAM E. HILL & SONS, London. L.O.B. 14 1/4" (362 mm), in case. The one-piece back of medium curl descending to the right, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll plain, the table of medium grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground. Excellent condition.

A VIOLIN by LEOPOLD BOURDOT, bearing the maker's manuscript label LUTHERIE D'ART A PARIS, No. 104, dated 1904. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), in case. The two-piece back of medium flame descending from the joint, the ribs of similar curl, the scroll of narrow curl, the table of medium grain, the varnish of a clear orange colour.

AN ATTRACTIVE FRENCH VIOLIN, bearing the label of HAWKES & SON, London, THE CONCERT VIOLIN, dated 1930. L.O.B. 14 1/4" (362 mm(, in case. The two-piece back of narrow flame, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain, the oil varnish slightly craquelled of a red colour on a yellow ground.

A VIOLIN by PAUL BAILLY, bearing the maker's label with signature: PUPIL OF JEAN BAPTISTE VUILLAUME, 86 Wardour Street, London. Dated 1891, Number 756, with the inscription on the inner back. L.O.B. 14 1/16" (357 mm), in case. The one-piece back of medium curl descending slightly to the right, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of even broad grain, the varnish of an orange-red-brown colour on a yellow ground. A small chip absent from the lower table flank edge, otherwise very good condition.
A SILVER-MOUNTED VIOLIN BOW, the ebony frog with pearl eye and rounded heel, the round stick of a red-brown colour. 59 grams.

A VIOLIN by PAUL BAILLY, bearing the maker's label PUPIL OF JEAN BAPTISTE VUILLAUME, 86 Wardour Street, London, c. 1890, No. 749, signed on the inner back. L.O.B. 14 1/16" (357 mm). The one-piece back of medium curl, ascending to the right, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of strong narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground.

A FINE VIOLIN by a maker of the PARIS SCHOOL, circa 1830-1840, bearing the label JOANNES FRANCISCUS PRESSENDA q RAPHAEL, fecit TAURINI, Anno Domini 1830. L.O.B. 14 3/16" (360 mm). The one-piece back of broad flame descending slightly from left to right, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of even broad slightly wavy grain, the varnish of a red colour on a yellow ground.

A FINE VIOLIN by HIPPOLYTE SILVESTRE, bearing the maker's label FAIT PAR HIPPOLYTE SILVESTRE A LYON EN 1866. L.O.B. 14 1/8" (359 mm), in shaped case. The one-piece back of medium curl, the ribs and scroll of similar curl, the table of narrow grain widening to the flanks, the varnish of a red-brown colour on a yellow ground. See Illustration Plate I

A FINE VIOLIN by LEANDRO BISIACH, bearing the maker's label DELLA SCUOLA CREMONESE, FECE IN MILANO, 1897, PIAZZA DEL DUOMO. L.O.B. 14 1/16" (357 mm), in shaped case. The one-piece back of medium curl ascending to the right, the ribs and scroll of similar figure, the table of medium grain, the transparent varnish of an orange colour on a yellow ground. With the certificate of MESSRS. L. P. BALMFORTH in Leeds, dated December 1937, stating that in our opinion it was made by LEANDRO BISIACH. See Illustration Plate II

AN IMPORTANT VIOLIN by JACOBUS STAINER, with a receipt and certificate of MESSRS. W. E. HILL & SONS, London, dated October 1929, stating:— We certify that the violin sold by us was made by JACOBUS STAINER of ABSAM and bears a label dated 1659. Description: The back is a jointed one of wood marked by a small curl, the sides matching, the head of fainter curl, the varnish of a golden colour, slightly browner on table. The instrument, which measures 13 15/16" (354 mm) in length of body, is a characteristic and well-preserved example of the maker's work. See Illustration Plate III · Ref. FRIDOLIN HAMMAH German Violin Makers. A similar example (on Plate 62) dated 1642. (A violin case and two bows included with the above lot.)

A SILVER-MOUNTED VIOLIN BOW by JAMES TUBBS, stamped JAS. TUBBS on the shaft. The ebony frog with silver adjuster, the round stick with silver face of a deep red-brown colour. Original ebony tongue and lapping. Fine condition. 58 grams.

AN INTERESTING SILVER-MOUNTED FRENCH VIOLIN BOW. The ebony frog with pearl eye and silver adjuster. The stick bearing the brand of H. GERMAIN A PARIS on the shaft and at the mortice, also E. SARTORY A PARIS under the lapping on both sides. The round stick of a red-brown colour. 54 grams (minus lapping).
A SILVER-MOUNTED VIOLIN BOW by EMILE OUCHARD, branded on the shaft. The ebony frog with pearl eye and ring, the round stick of a medium brown shade. 62 grams.

A SILVER-MOUNTED VIOLIN BOW by JOHN & ARTHUR BEARE, stamped on the shaft. The ebony frog with pearl eye and ring, the octagonal stick of a light brown colour. 51 grams (minus hair). With a pinewood bow-box. (2)

A SILVER-MOUNTED VIOLONCELLO BOW by W. E. HILL & SONS, stamped W. E. HILL & SONS on the shaft. The round stick of a red-brown colour, the adjuster of silver with ivory sandwich, the ebony frog with silver ferrule, may be a later Hill adaption. Minus hair. 72 grams. With bow-box, lined velvet. (2)

A SILVER-MOUNTED VIOLONCELLO BOW by W. E. HILL & SONS, stamped W.E.H.&S. on the shaft. The round stick of a red-brown colour, the ebony frog with silver ferrule and adjuster. 67 grams. Minus hair.
A NICKEL-MOUNTED VIOLONCELLO BOW, stamped DODD on the shaft. The ebony frog with nickel ferrule and adjuster. 66 grams. Minus hair.
A GOOD SILVER-MOUNTED VIOLA BOW by W. E. HILL & SONS, stamped W.E.H.&S. on the shaft. The ebony frog with full mounts and adjuster, the round stick of a red-brown colour. 67 grams.
A GOOD SILVER-MOUNTED VIOLONCELLO BOW, bearing the brand of CHANOT on the shaft. The ebony frog with pearl eye and ring, the octagonal stick of a red-brown colour. 80 grams.
A VIOLIN BOW attributed to J. B. VUILLAUME, circa 1840, unslamped. The stick of hollow steel, the ebony frog with silver mounts and pearl eye, without upper plate.
Two SILVER-MOUNTED VIOLIN BOWS (one stamped DODD on the shaft).

A VIOLONCELLO BOW, probably English, with silver-mounted ebony frog, the adjuster nickel, the stick octagonal of a red-brown colour; and A NICKEL-MOUNTED VIOLONCELLO BOW, stamped VUILLAUME A PARIS on the shaft, the ivory frog with pearl eye and ring, the stick of a light red colour. (2)
THREE NICKEL-MOUNTED VIOLIN BOWS (one stamped OUCHARD on the shaft). (3)
A SILVER-MOUNTED VIOLA BOW (a repair, and winding near the head); and A VIOLIN BOW, stamped M. WERNER on the shaft. (2)
